message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Marvin Gardens.

I have $889 and a dark blue monopoly. I own Atlantic Avenue, Pacific Avenue, and Boardwalk. Player 4 has Ventnor and the green set. Marvin Gardens is the only remaining yellow property.

The auction is at $82 with p1 leading. I am weighing whether to continue bidding for Ventnor, which would give me two of three yellows. Player 4 is broke and has no cash to bid back. I need to balance the value of completing the yellow set against preserving enough cash to survive a large rent hit.

Marvin Gardens has a $140 mortgage value. A bid under that amount nets positive cash if mortgaged immediately. I am now weighing the strategic value of holding the property.

Player 4 is nearly broke with only $29 and heavily invested in hotels on Med/Baltic. Player 1 has $320 but sits in jail; his orange set with houses poses a serious rent threat. I am calculating whether the orange rent danger justifies continuing the bid.

Standard Monopoly rent tables show New York Avenue with three houses pays $600, and Virginia with three houses pays $500. These figures are being used to assess the rent threat from Player 1.

Player 2 has built three houses on Virginia Avenue and three on States Avenue. St. Charles Place has two houses.

Player 2's three houses on St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue generate $150, $450, and $500 in rent respectively.

I am not on the spaces that generate rent from Player 2. Paying $83 for Marvin would leave me with $806 cash. The $140 mortgage value is only "free money" if I do not need to unmortgage soon, since that costs $154 including interest. I also see that owning Marvin blocks others from completing a yellow monopoly, though no opponent currently holds two yellows.

Marvin Gardens is uniquely valuable to me as the path to a yellow monopoly. Player 1 buying it would only serve as a mortgage chip and a denial against me, since it cannot complete their set. I will bid $83 and continue with one-dollar steps rather than jumping to end the auction.

Player 1 may drop out soon or bid to $140. They still have $180 left after that, so they might want Marvin as a trade chip against me. I will bid $83 and keep the public message brief without showing a ceiling.
